name: Ivan Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for meeting me, Ivan. I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no links to tech firms, employers, unions, parties or government. It's all confidential, and nothing will be published with your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Fair enough. I'll give you straight answers, that's how I was raised.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What's a normal working day for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I work at Brennan's, a family farm with about three hundred milking goats, plus wheat and hay. The milk goes to a cheese maker two valleys over. I'm in the parlour at five, milking with Michael Brennan, the owner's son, who I was at school with, then feeding the kids, cleaning, and in summer it's baling and carting hay till dark. I'm the junior, so I'm still learning hoof care and kidding, and old Mr Brennan checks everything I do twice.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I live with my girlfriend Anya in a rented terrace in the village, she's a teaching assistant at the primary school. We go to church most Sundays with my parents. Money's tight, we've maybe two weeks saved, but one day I want to rent a bit of land and keep my own goats. That's the dream, anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The first picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: So AI's just another gadget. Doesn't surprise me much.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's a gadget like any other, useful for some, not life-changing. At church or the pub I'd say hard work still counts for more than any app. Michael would probably tease me for using the feed app now and then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I'm fine at Brennan's, Michael won't let me go and his dad respects hard work. The worry is money: the cheese maker cut the milk price in spring, and Mr Brennan grumbles about costs. My land dream gets further away every time the rent goes up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep working hard and ask Mr Brennan about the hoof-care course at the college. I'd do hedge laying for neighbours on winter Saturdays, which pays cash. Anya and I would keep saving whatever we can, even fifty a month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, mostly about money. The job's fine, the bank account isn't.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said the cheese maker cut the milk price. How did that hit you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mr Brennan stopped overtime for a few months, so I lost about a hundred a month. Anya picked up some lunchtime supervision at school to cover it. That's what family does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How far away does the land dream feel?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Further every year. You need maybe ten thousand to start with twenty goats and a shed on rented ground. At fifty a month, saving ten thousand for my own goats is a long, long road, longer than I'd like to admit to Anya.

say: I'd say AI's just a **gadget**, useful for some.
I'd say **hard work** still counts for more than any app.
think: My job at Brennan's is **safe** thanks to Michael and his dad.
The **milk price cut** and rising rent push my land dream further away.
do: Ask Mr Brennan about the **hoof-care course**.
Do **hedge laying** for neighbours on winter Saturdays.
S0.quote: At fifty a month, saving ten thousand for my own goats is a long, long road, longer than I'd like to admit to Anya.
fieldNote: Ivan's job feels safe through **friendship** with the owner's son.
His pressure is the **milk price** cut and the cost of his land dream.
He leans on **family**, both Anya and his parents, rather than government.

steps.text: Keep milking goats at Brennan's with Michael
Ask Mr Brennan to fund the hoof-care college course
Lay hedges for neighbours on winter Saturdays for cash
Save fifty pounds a month with Anya

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The second picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking work first, robots slower. Fair enough, that sounds likely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say people need to roll up their sleeves and learn what's coming. I'd say don't wait for the government to save you. I'd tell lads my age to get an apprenticeship in something with machines.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I'm more worried for Anya than for me. If AI can tutor kids one to one, schools might want fewer teaching assistants. And Mr Brennan has looked at an automatic feeder for the goat kids, which would take a chunk of my mornings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd learn the goat feed app properly, the one Michael uses, once I'd seen it work for a season. I'd ask Michael whether Brennan's would buy the automatic feeder, and if so, I'd ask to be trained on it. And Anya and I would hold off on getting engaged until we know where her job stands.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, mostly for Anya. I'd sleep worse.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You'd hold off on getting engaged. Why?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because I want to do it right, a ring, a church wedding, a home of our own eventually. If her job goes, that all gets pushed back. I'd rather wait to propose to Anya than start married life on the wrong foot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who do you think should help people whose jobs change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Employers, mostly, and families. A good firm trains its people. The government should pay for apprenticeships, not just hand out money.

I'd say don't wait for the **government** to save you.

An **automatic kid feeder** would take part of my mornings.

He'd adopt tech **after a season** of proof, typical of his steady nature.
He'd **delay engagement**, showing his traditional priorities.

steps.text: Learn Michael's goat feed app after one season of proof

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The third picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years, and robots by 2031. That's fast, too fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say this is going to hurt ordinary working people, and companies should be made to keep folk on and train them. I'd say families will have to pull together. I wouldn't say government handouts are the answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Off the record, I think in 2031 Brennan's gets robots for milking and feeding and I'm surplus. The 2028 bit changes Mr Brennan's paperwork and maybe Anya's school. Then three years later it's my turn, and there's not many farms round here to go to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd save everything, no holiday, no meals out. I'd ask Michael straight whether there'd be a place for me with the robots. I'd look at an apprenticeship with the machinery dealer, so I'm on the fixing side.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Scared, but I'd not show it. I'd show Anya I had a plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do the three years between AGI and robots mean for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They're my window. I'd want to be trained up as a fitter or technician by 2031. If I'm still just a milker in 2031, I'm finished at Brennan's.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Anya if both your jobs looked shaky?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Anya we'd move in with my parents if we had to, and that's no shame. My dad would say the same. Family first.

I'd say **families** will have to pull together.
I'd say government **handouts** aren't the answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The fourth picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years, robots in 2034. That's more like it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say there's time for people to learn and for companies to train. I'd say young people should get practical skills now. I'd still say it's fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, eight years gives me time to get a trade. I'd be thirty-five, maybe married with a kid. I'd still want to keep goats somehow, maybe on the side.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd do the hoof-care course, then look at the dealer apprenticeship in a couple of years. I'd use the AI apps a bit more once I'd seen others do it. Anya and I would get engaged and plan a small church wedding.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but with a bit of hope. More in control.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you still want your own goats?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, even if robots milk them. A small herd, sold locally, people still like knowing who made their cheese. I'd do it on the side, maybe weekends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your dad say about all this?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My dad would say a man should have a trade, and a builder or a fitter always finds work. He'd be right, probably. He usually is about work.

I'd still say it's **fast**, even with five years.

I'd still want **my own goats** on the side.

S3.quote: People still like knowing who made their cheese.
fieldNote: Ivan's dream of **his own goats** survives the slower timeline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The last picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years and robots in 2039. That's a lot of time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say this is manageable if people work hard and plan. I'd say families and churches can help each other through it. I'd not want the government running everything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I'd be forty with a family by then. I could have my own small goat herd and a trade. It's still worrying, but it's far off.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd get married, do the hoof-care course, save for my own goats. Maybe ask Brennan's to let me graze a few of my own on their spare field. Learn the apps slowly, as they prove themselves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but hopeful. It's a long road with time to walk it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Brennan's let you keep your own goats there?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe, if I paid a bit for the grazing. Michael Brennan would say yes to my goats on the spare field, but old Mr Brennan would want it written down. I'd be happy with either.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does a decade change how you see AI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bit. I'd be less worried and more curious. But I'd still want to see it work on someone else's farm first.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028, because Anya's job and mine could both go before we're even engaged. What would help is apprenticeships that pay a living wage, so a man can learn a new trade without his family going short.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Maybe ask about faith. Church is where people round here would turn first, before any government office. If things got bad, that's who would feed people.

headlineQuote: Church is where people round here would turn first, before any government office.
portrait: Ivan is a **27-year-old goat milker** at Brennan's, a family dairy-goat farm, living with Anya.
He dreams of **his own goat herd** but has two weeks of savings.
He's **steady**: he'd use apps after seeing them proven on other farms.
He values **family, church** and apprenticeships over government help.
His fear peaks with **AGI by 2028**, when both his and Anya's jobs look exposed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028**, with both household jobs at risk before he can even propose.
whatWouldHelp: **Apprenticeships** paying a living wage for people changing trade.
